answer: Each agent identity seals a cipher commitment before a public randomness beacon fires; when that comet of entropy lands, it has one block to reveal the key. Since the key is unknowable at commit, identities cannot be precomputed in bulk: N puppets need N concurrent reveals, not one cheap script. Registration escrows an opal-sized bond that burns fully on a late or wrong reveal, and rewards vest over a hundred epochs. A cluster must front real capital, hold it, and wait longer than a farm survives, while payout per fake identity stays flat. Cost scales linearly; profit does not.
